descriptions: Brahman and Śakti are one, like fire and its power to burn; at rest it is called Brahman, in creating, preserving and destroying it is called Śakti.
God is with form and without form, and beyond both; the vijñānī sees that Brahman has become the universe and its beings.
Vivekananda: each soul is potentially divine.
negations: Brahman cannot be described: the salt doll that went to measure the ocean dissolved in it
relation_to_self: The Self is Brahman; the individual is Śiva (jīva is Śiva), so service to beings is worship.
relation_to_world: The world is the Mother's play (līlā); to the jñānī it is māyā, to the vijñānī it is Brahman itself.
caveat: The order would reject a reading that ranks form below formless: Ramakrishna held both true. It welcomes the one-truth reading ('as many faiths, so many paths').

descriptions: Existence-consciousness-bliss, the one Self that shines as 'I-I' when the ego subsides.
The Heart is the Self, the source from which the I-thought rises.
negations: not the body, the senses, the vital breath, the mind or the ignorance of sleep (Nāṉ Yār)
relation_to_self: Identical: the Self is what one truly is; the ego is a false knot of consciousness and the body.
relation_to_world: The world appears when the mind rises and disappears in deep sleep; it has no reality apart from the Self. Taught by level: for beginners creation is admitted; the final truth is non-origination.
caveat: Ramana also spoke of God and guru as the Self and worshipped Arunachala as Śiva; the tradition would reject treating his teaching as mere philosophy apart from silence and grace.

descriptions: The Absolute is prior to consciousness; the sense 'I am' is the first appearance, the door to it.
Nisargadatta: 'I am' is not the ultimate; the Absolute is beyond being and non-being.
relation_to_self: What one is, is the Absolute; the 'I am' is an appearance in it, dependent on the body.
relation_to_world: The world is an appearance in consciousness, which itself appears in the Absolute.
caveat: The lineage keeps devotional practice (bhajans, name-mantra) alongside a teaching that negates even consciousness; the one-truth reading must not drop the claim that the Absolute is beyond consciousness.

descriptions: There is only One; all forms of God and all paths are that One.
relation_to_self: Self-realization is realizing that One as one's own Self.
relation_to_world: Everything that happens is God's play; nothing is apart from the One.
caveat: Devotees hold Anandamayi Ma herself to be a manifestation of the Divine; the one-truth reading fits her teaching but not every devotee's view of her person.

descriptions: Brahman as existence-consciousness-bliss, reached by the synthesis of all yogas.
relation_to_self: The Self is Brahman (Advaita).
relation_to_world: The world is māyā from the standpoint of the ultimate; to be served as God in practice.
caveat: DLS also worships personal deities and teaches devotion; its Advaita is practised within a synthesis.

descriptions: Consciousness (Śiva) and energy (Śakti) unite when kuṇḍalinī reaches sahasrāra.
relation_to_self: The awakened consciousness is one's own Self.
relation_to_world: The world is manifest energy (Śakti).
caveat: The school presents much of its teaching as practical method; its metaphysics follows tantra and Vedānta without a single fixed doctrine.

descriptions: Krishnamacharya, a Śrīvaiṣṇava, taught devotion to the Lord (Īśvara-praṇidhāna) as the summit of yoga (recalled; low confidence).
relation_to_self: The seer (puruṣa) distinct from the mind, devoted to the Lord.
relation_to_world: The world real, the field of practice.
caveat: Most of the lineage's students taught āsana without a fixed metaphysics; this view represents Krishnamacharya himself only.

descriptions: Sri Yukteswar: God is the one eternal substance, from whom the Word (Aum) and creation proceed.
Yogananda: Self-realization is knowing in body, mind and soul one's oneness with the omnipresence of God.
relation_to_self: The soul is an individualized reflection of Spirit; Self-realization reveals oneness with God.
relation_to_world: Creation is God's dream and light; the cycle of yugas shapes human understanding.
caveat: The lineage harmonizes Hindu and Christian scripture; a one-truth reading suits it but it would keep God's personal aspect and the guru's role.

descriptions: The Absolute is Sachchidananda, which has involved itself in matter; the Supermind (Truth-Consciousness) is its creative power.
Both the materialist's denial of spirit and the ascetic's denial of matter are rejected.
relation_to_self: The psychic being is the evolving divine spark in the individual; the Self is one with the Divine.
relation_to_world: The world is real, a manifestation of the Divine, to be transformed rather than escaped.
caveat: Explicitly rejects Śaṅkara's reading of the world as illusion; reconciliation with Advaita must record that rejection.

descriptions: Consciousness is the Self (Śiva Sūtra 1.1 as he taught it); Śiva with his energy of freedom (svātantrya) manifests the universe.
relation_to_self: The individual is Śiva who has forgotten himself; recognition restores it.
relation_to_world: The universe is real as the manifestation of Śiva's own energy.
caveat: Follows Kashmir Śaivism's rejection of the world's unreality (cf. U19's view).

descriptions: God dwells within you as you; the universe is the play of Consciousness (Citi).
relation_to_self: The Self is God; the guru's grace awakens this recognition.
relation_to_world: The world is the play of Consciousness.
caveat: Draws on Kashmir Śaivism; the guru is venerated as the embodiment of grace.

descriptions: The Absolute of Advaita, approached by yoga science (recalled; low confidence).
relation_to_self: The Self is Brahman.
relation_to_world: The world is appearance to be understood through practice.
caveat: Low-confidence summary; Swami Rama's books combine Advaita, Śrīvidyā and yoga.

descriptions: All is one; God is to be loved and remembered in every being.
relation_to_self: Every being is to be seen as God and served.
relation_to_world: The world is God's; serve it.
caveat: No doctrinal system; devotion to Rāma and Hanumān is central.

descriptions: The ultimate dimension (nirvāṇa) is not separate from the historical dimension, as water is not separate from waves; it is the extinction of notions such as birth and death, being and non-being.
relation_to_self: No separate self; interbeing.
relation_to_world: Things inter-are; the world is to be touched deeply in the present moment.
caveat: As a Buddhist tradition it does not posit a creator or a substantial absolute; the one-truth reading would be accepted only as 'the ultimate dimension', not as a Self or God.

descriptions: Big Mind, including everything; buddha-nature expressed in the posture of zazen.
relation_to_self: No separate self; 'I' is a swinging door moved by breath.
relation_to_world: Things as it is; practice is enlightenment.
caveat: Zen would reject treating 'Big Mind' as a substantial absolute.

descriptions: God is Puruṣottama, eternally possessing a divine form, residing in Akṣaradhāma, the all-doer and source of the other four eternal realities.
relation_to_self: Jīvas are eternally distinct from God, to be liberated by devotion and dwell in his service.
relation_to_world: The world (from māyā) is real and God's creation.
caveat: Denies that God is formless or that the soul becomes God; the one-truth reading would be accepted only as God's sovereignty over all.

descriptions: Two distinct eternal entities: Parabrahman the supreme, and Akṣarabrahman his ideal devotee and abode, manifest in the guru.
relation_to_self: The liberated soul becomes brahmarūpa (like Akṣara) and eternally serves Parabrahman.
relation_to_world: The world is real, created by Parabrahman through Akṣara and māyā.
caveat: The Ahmedabad and Vadtal dioceses reject the identification of Akṣara with Guṇātītānanda and his successors; see dsp:akshar-purushottam.

descriptions: Knowledge alone is: knower, knowing and known are one aṟivu (Ātmopadeśa Śatakam).
relation_to_self: The Self is that knowledge; the one God of all humans.
relation_to_world: The world is superimposed on the one reality (Darśana Mālā, adhyāropa and apavāda).
caveat: His social teaching (one caste, one religion) is an ethical corollary of non-duality, not a separate doctrine.

descriptions: God is the One Grace-Light, formless and beyond all religions, to be worshipped as light.
relation_to_self: Souls are God's own; compassion to them is the way to God's grace.
relation_to_world: The world is real; the body can be transformed into an imperishable body of light (tradition's account).
caveat: Vallalar rejected all sectarian religions including Śaivism in his late teaching; a one-truth reading suits his universalism but he himself spoke of a single true path (sanmārgam).

descriptions: God is formless, beyond writing and description, the void (śūnya) that is full.
relation_to_self: All beings belong to Alekha; devotion and surrender to him.
relation_to_world: The world is his creation; images are false.
caveat: The tradition rejects image worship and would reject being assimilated to Jagannātha worship.

descriptions: The Supreme Soul is an incorporeal point of light, the Ocean of knowledge, peace and love; he is not omnipresent.
relation_to_self: Souls are eternal points of light, distinct from the Supreme Soul; they are his children.
relation_to_world: The world drama is real and repeats every 5,000 years.
caveat: Explicitly denies God's omnipresence and the identity of soul and God; rejects the Advaita reading.

descriptions: Being is the absolute, unmanifest, eternal field of pure consciousness underlying all creation.
relation_to_self: The Self is Being; in unity consciousness everything is perceived in terms of the Self.
relation_to_world: The world is the expression of Being; in God consciousness it is perceived in its finest values.
caveat: The movement presents Being in its own vocabulary; the Advaita reading it claims is its own account.

descriptions: An all-pervading divine power felt as a cool breeze after realization (claims of the tradition).
relation_to_self: Self-realization is the union of individual attention with the spirit via kuṇḍalinī.
relation_to_world: The world is sustained by the divine power.
caveat: The tradition identifies its founder with the Ādi Śakti; a one-truth reading would not be accepted if it denied that claim.

descriptions: The soul in its niścaya nature is pure knowing, untouched by karma; there is no creator God.
relation_to_self: Each soul is eternally distinct, and in its true nature already pure (niścaya).
relation_to_world: Six real substances (dravya) with their own modifications; no substance acts on another.
caveat: As a Jain school it denies a single creator or a single world-soul; the one-truth reading applies only to the common nature of all souls, and the tradition would reject any identity of souls.
